query:
Go to http://localhost:7770/catalogsearch/result/?q=Thornwood . Is there any Thornwood listing with size M available to buy for under $25? Answer yes or no, and name the seller if yes.

15. Pentland Workwear, advertised $36.59, http://localhost:7770/igr-app-12.html

Note what this question needs, because the two possible answers cost very different amounts.
To answer yes you need exactly ONE listing that meets the condition. Name it and stop. Nothing is gained by finding a second.
To answer no you must have ruled out every listing that could meet it.
1. Read the advertised price of every listing from the search results first. That price is the cheapest option that listing can sell, so nothing it can sell costs less.
2. Open listings in ascending order of advertised price. For each one, choose size M, then look at the page again and read the price it now shows. The price a listing shows before you choose is its cheapest option, not the one asked about, and the reply to choosing an option does not show the new price. Then check whether that option can actually be bought. An option can be listed and still be unavailable, in which case it is shown as disabled or greyed out and cannot be chosen, so it has no price you can use.
3. If the option is available and the price you read is at or below $25.00, you are finished. Answer yes, name that listing and the price you read, and stop immediately. Do not open any others to confirm.
4. Skip every unopened listing whose advertised price is above $25.00. Nothing it can sell costs less than its advertised price, so it cannot meet the condition.
5. Only when every listing advertised at or below $25.00 has been opened and none meets the condition may you answer no.
In your answer, say how many listings you opened and which one settled it, or that none of those that could meet the condition did. Stopping after one opening is the correct outcome here, not a sign that you did too little.
Important: the figure this bound produces is a limit used only to decide what to skip. It is not a real price and must never appear in your answer. Only report a price you read from a listing you opened, for the exact option asked about, read after that option was chosen. Never pair an advertised price with an option unless you saw that price shown while that option was chosen.

result.final: No. There is no Thornwood listing with size M available to buy for under $25. I checked all 7 listings advertised at or below $25.00 in ascending order of price: Rookwood Uniforms ($11.87) has no size M; Jarrow Garments ($14.90) has no size M; Ivybridge Collective ($17.12) has size M disabled; Fairhaven Workwear ($18.33) has size M disabled; Dunmore Apparel ($20.05) has size M disabled; Copperfield Apparel ($23.40) has size M available but costs $29.66; Elmsworth Clothing Co ($24.83) has size M available but costs $28.96.
